# Patched bundled SQLite with the existing rusqlite API

Based on the published `rusqlite` 0.37.0 crate, upstream
<https://github.com/rusqlite/rusqlite>, commit
`44e0ef965580b94d59c5dfe8874b57ab5993a8f7`.
The registry archive SHA-256 is
`165ca6e57b20e1351573e3729b958bc62f0e48025386970b6e4d29e7a7e71f3f`.
The upstream MIT license, source, tests, original manifest, and commit
provenance are retained. The unused package lockfile is omitted; the
application and fuzz workspace lockfiles resolve their dependencies.

The only production change is the normalized manifest's `libsqlite3-sys`
requirement: 0.35.0 becomes 0.39.1. This uses the official registry release,
which bundles SQLite 3.54.1 and fixes
[RUSTSEC-2026-0459](https://github.com/RustSec/advisory-db/blob/main/crates/libsqlite3-sys/RUSTSEC-2026-0459.md)
(CVE-2026-119375). No SQLite code or wrapper implementation is changed here,
and the package retains its actual 0.37.0 version.

An ordinary rusqlite 0.41 upgrade is currently blocked: tor-dirmgr 0.47.0
and 0.48.0 require rusqlite below 0.41, while the latest r2d2_sqlite 0.35.0
requires rusqlite 0.40. Keeping the existing wrapper API avoids changing
those upstream libraries. SQLite's C API supplies the same calls used by
this wrapper. The dependency's Rust minimum is 1.88, below this project's
toolchains.

All application SQLite consumers enable `bundled`; the patched registry
dependency therefore supplies their SQLite implementation on desktop and
mobile. An external `LIBSQLITE3_SYS_USE_PKG_CONFIG` override still selects
the system library and requires that library to be patched separately.
The unbundled upstream mode now requires SQLite 3.45.3 or newer. SQLCipher
is not enabled by this workspace; this patch makes no claim that an
externally supplied SQLite or SQLCipher is fixed.

Validation uses the existing rusqlite tests with `bundled,hooks,time`, the
application database and EVX state tests, workspace/mobile feature
resolution, and the unchanged security scanner policies. The fuzz
workspace applies the same patch so its SQLite version matches shipping
code. To run the wrapper tests:

```sh
cargo test --manifest-path vendor/rusqlite/Cargo.toml --lib --features bundled,hooks,time
```

Remove the standalone vendor lockfile generated by that command after
testing. Remove this patch when the Tor and connection-pool dependencies
support an upstream rusqlite release using patched SQLite, after passing
the same compatibility checks.
